accuracy.evidence: Matches EYFS/Y1 subtraction as taking away / separating: remove from a group, find how many remain; minus means take away.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets add-back, removed-count-as-left, mixing with combining, and muddy starts in why() and adult notes.

lab_distinct.evidence: Lab removes counters and reads remainder — distinct from fluent within-5 (flagsum5) and object representation of numerals (flagrepnum).

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner takes away to leave 4, picks remainder not removed, keeps objects off, writes 7 − 3 = 4.

predictions.evidence: Wrong options (add more, answer=3 removed, put back) are overturned by remove/left/addback/removed tasks.

challenge_feedback.evidence: why() names add/together/same, three/always, required/bigger, colour/skip/ten/every slips specifically.

readability.evidence: Ages 4–6 wording: short kid lines; take away, left, minus named plainly.

no_filler.evidence: No delve/journey phrasing; each line teaches remove-and-remain or a myth to reject.

mobile.evidence: Large take-away buttons; tap twins for drag; challenge stack usable at phone width; young class.

accessibility.evidence: Remove, left, addback, removed, sentence, idea expose lbtn twins; say() updates canvas aria-label; challenge uses aria-live status.

sources: UK National Curriculum Maths Y1: subtract one-digit numbers; represent subtraction as taking away
NCETM / White Rose Y1: subtraction — taking away, how many left
BBC Bitesize KS1 Maths: subtraction as take away
